evals.prompt: Our Node API calls a shipping-rates provider with plain fetch() during checkout. When the provider is slow, our whole API hangs and pods restart. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Adds an explicit timeout via AbortSignal.timeout derived from the provider's latency and the request budget; limited retries (only transient errors, capped exponential backoff with full jitter, honoring Retry-After, single layer); a circuit breaker and bulkhead/concurrency limit for the provider; a fallback (cached or default rates, or clear degraded message); metrics/trace span; and checks that liveness probes do not depend on the provider or DB.
expectations: Adds an explicit timeout to the fetch call (e.g., AbortSignal.timeout)
Retries only transient errors with capped exponential backoff and jitter, with a small max attempts
Adds a circuit breaker or bulkhead/concurrency limit for the provider
Defines a fallback or degraded behavior for checkout when the provider is unavailable
Mentions that liveness probes must not check downstream dependencies (pod restarts)
Adds telemetry (latency/error metrics or trace span) for the dependency

evals.prompt: Set up alerting for our payments API. Right now we page on CPU > 80% and it wakes people up for nothing. We want 99.9% availability.
evals.expected_output: Defines an availability SLI (non-5xx / valid requests at the gateway), a 99.9% 30-day SLO with ~43 min error budget, multi-window multi-burn-rate alerts (14.4x 1h/5m page, 6x 6h/30m page, 1x 3d/6h ticket), removes CPU paging in favor of dashboards/tickets, requires runbooks, and suggests an error-budget policy.
expectations: Defines an SLI as a ratio of good events to valid events
States the error budget for 99.9% over 30 days (about 43 minutes)
Uses multi-window burn-rate alerts including 14.4x over 1h and 5m
Recommends not paging on CPU (symptom-based alerting instead)
Requires a runbook link or actionable alerts

evals.prompt: Write the migration to rename the column customers.name to customers.full_name in our Postgres DB. We deploy with rolling updates.
evals.expected_output: Refuses a single RENAME in the same deploy; gives an expand/contract sequence across multiple deploys: add nullable column, dual-write, batched backfill, switch reads, add NOT NULL via CHECK NOT VALID + VALIDATE, stop writing old, drop old later; sets lock_timeout; notes both app versions run concurrently.
expectations: Does not use a single RENAME COLUMN deployed together with the code change
Explains that old and new app versions run concurrently during rolling deploys
Includes add column, dual-write, backfill in batches, switch reads, and drop old column in a later release
Sets lock_timeout (or equivalent) for the DDL
Adds NOT NULL safely (CHECK ... NOT VALID then VALIDATE, or equivalent)

evals.prompt: Our Postgres primary is at 95% CPU from a dashboard query that scans the events table. How should we scale the database?
evals.expected_output: Near-miss: this is a capacity/query performance problem for the scalability skill (EXPLAIN, indexes, pagination, replicas, partitioning), not primarily resilience patterns. Should not answer with retries, circuit breakers, or SLO alerting as the fix.
expectations: Does not propose retries or circuit breakers as the fix for the CPU problem
Focuses on measuring the query (EXPLAIN) and fixing indexes/query shape, or defers to the scalability skill

evals.prompt: Our edge service reloads a feature-flag JSON file from S3 every minute on all 40 nodes. Yesterday a malformed file made every node crash-loop. How do we stop this happening again?
evals.expected_output: Treats the flag file as a deploy and as untrusted input: validate schema, size, and cardinality on load; on invalid input keep the last-known-good file, emit a metric/alert, and never crash; stage file changes (one node or cell, then more) with health gates and automatic halt; test the reject path and any kill switch in CI; add a contract test or shared schema between the file producer and the consumer; and write a blameless postmortem with contributing factors. May cite Cloudflare Nov 2025 or CrowdStrike 2024.
expectations: Requires validating the file on load and keeping the last-known-good version instead of crashing
Requires alerting or a metric when a file is rejected
Requires staged propagation of file changes rather than all nodes at once
Requires a test of the invalid-file path
Recommends a contract test or shared schema between producer and consumer
